newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-INJURY WORRY OVER IEUAN EVANS FOR TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-INJURY WORRY OVER IEUAN EVANS FOR TEST.

text.p: The fitness of veteran Welsh wing Ieuan Evans is worrying the British Lions ahead of the second test against South Africa at Kings Park on Saturday.
Evans -- the most experienced Lion in the 35-man party with seven appearances spread over 1989, 1993 and 1997 -- is suffering from a recurring groin strain.

"There is certainly a question mark over Ieuan with his groin injury. He felt it a bit during the first test on Saturday and he's a concern for the second test here in Durban," Lions manager Fran Cotton told a news conference on Wednesday.
"We'll be getting medical opinion from the team doctor (James Robson) this evening and we'll make a final decision tonight."
Cotton said the Lions team for the second test would be picked on Wednesday evening but would only be announced to the media early on Thursday afternoon.

"We haven't picked the team yet but we will only consider players who are 110 percent fit - we don't want any injury doubts. Saturday's second test is going to be a monumental match and there's no doubt in my mind that the forwad battle will be a lot more intense than it was at Newlands."
Lions coach Ian McGeechan admitted team selection for Kings Park would be based on the 15 players who drew first blood against South Africa in Cape Town by a 25-16 margin.

"We'll take Saturday's team as a template - it would be stupid not to," he said. "But the way the players played in Bloemfontein last night...you genuinely have to look at them, assess them and review them."
Cotton said there would be a replacement for English centre Will Greenwood, who was concussed during the Lions' emphatic 52-30 win over Free State on Tuesday.
Cotton said Greenwood, apart from his concussion, had also dislocated his shoulder.

"He (Will) will remain here in South Africa until at least Monday. He will then rely on medical opinion as to when he should fly home. Our doctor James Robson recommends he should then sensibly consider a two-month lay-off from the game."
